criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The introduction establishes a strong, well-justified mission concept addressing coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef using fluid lensing. It explains why dedicated monitoring is needed, justifies using a single spacecraft, and identifies relevant Australian stakeholders and operators (CSIRO, BOM, universities).

evidence.quote: Thus, only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications, reduces cost, and requires less time

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All key design segments are addressed, including orbital elements, launch rideshare, STK access analysis, and EOL disposal. However, claiming an equatorial launch assists a retrograde Sun-Synchronous Orbit is an orbital-mechanics error. Additionally, EOL drag sail claims lack quantitative sizing or delta-V calculations.

evidence.quote: The most efficient rocket launches are from locations close to the equator as this is where maximum rotational velocity can be experienced

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion summarizes the core mission design selections—launch vehicle, orbit type, ground station, and operational utility—synthesizing the evidence presented in the report into appropriate final remarks.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report follows a clear structure with an executive summary. However, presentation suffers from unnumbered and uncaptioned figures, an incomplete sentence in the EOL section, poorly formatted raw URLs, and citing Wikipedia against explicit instructions.

technical_issues.issue: Equatorial launch sites provide a positive velocity boost only for prograde orbits; for a retrograde SSO (i = 97.79 deg), Earth rotation must be overcome.
Truncated text / incomplete sentence: 'utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable for low-earth orbit altitudes [10].'
Reference [6] cites Wikipedia, explicitly prohibited in the assignment brief.
Figures and tables lack standard academic numbering and formal captions.

overall: A solid mission concept tailored to Australian environmental needs with good use of STK for orbit access analysis. The report is held back by referencing Wikipedia, formatting lapses, an incomplete sentence in the EOL section, and an orbital mechanics misconception regarding equatorial launch benefits for retrograde orbits.

feedback.summary: You presented a well-motivated mission concept addressing Great Barrier Reef coral monitoring, supported by effective STK access modeling and a clear operational rationale. Your proposal addresses key Australian stakeholder needs well. To raise your design to the highest level, correct the orbital mechanics misconception regarding equatorial launches for retrograde orbits, substantiate your end-of-life disposal with quantitative calculations, and refine presentation standards by adding figure captions, fixing truncated text, and replacing prohibited sources like Wikipedia.
next_steps: Re-evaluate the launch site analysis by accounting for the velocity penalty incurred when launching into a retrograde Sun-Synchronous Orbit (i = 97.79°).
Substantiate the end-of-life disposal section with quantitative engineering calculations, such as required drag sail surface area or de-orbit delta-V.

Standardise report presentation by formally numbering and captioning all figures and tables, completing the truncated sentence in Mission Duration & EOL, and replacing Wikipedia with peer-reviewed references.

You effectively rationalised using a single satellite and identified key stakeholders like CSIRO and BOM. To reach the top of Accomplished, provide deeper quantitative mission rationale supporting your coverage requirements.

To achieve Accomplished, correct the orbital mechanics misconception regarding equatorial launch assistance for a retrograde Sun-Synchronous Orbit (i = 97.79°), and provide supporting quantitative sizing or delta-V calculations for the EOL drag sail.
criteria.C3: You successfully synthesised your design selections—including orbit type, launch vehicle, and ground stations—linking them back to operational utility. To improve within Accomplished, summarize the quantitative performance outcomes of your STK analysis and explicitly state how these confirm mission success criteria.
criteria.C4: You structured the report logically with a clear executive summary. To reach Accomplished, ensure all figures and tables in Orbit include formal numbering and captions, resolve the truncated sentence in Mission Duration & EOL, format references professionally, and remove non-academic sources like Wikipedia (Reference [6]).
